description: Reference choreography from the @ab3l.t TikTok (13.7 s of content; the 17.7 s clip ends with a TikTok end card). Group of four at night, waist-up framing; main dancer = tracker id 1 (centre, black hoodie), ids 2 and 4 dance the same choreography. Move boundaries from the wrist/elbow trajectories and motion energy of data/dance/pose/ab3lt_5d8bb1.npz plus frame strips of the annotated video (see docs/DANCE_MODEL_INTERFACE.md section 4 for the schema).
bpm_estimate_note: Estimated from the intro bounce (0.8-5.5 s): shoulder-bounce autocorrelation peaks at 0.73 s (r=0.89) and the hip side-to-side sway at 1.47 s (r=0.94), i.e. one bounce per beat at ~82 BPM. The track could equally be 164 BPM with the bounce every two beats; the arm moves from 6.6 s onward fall roughly on the 0.73 s grid.

moves.name: Ready: fists come up to the chest, elbows bent, standing close to the camera
Fists held at the chest, elbows bent, bouncing on the beat while stepping backwards away from the camera
In place: fists stay at the chest, bouncing on the beat with a side-to-side weight shift
Forearms cross in front of the chest, then both arms swing down and open out to the sides
Right hand rises to the side of the head, then the left hand joins so both hands are up by the head with elbows out
Arms drop; the right arm sweeps across the chest and back, then reaches straight up overhead, then both arms drop to the sides
Both hands come together at the left shoulder (left hand drops to the hip), then both hands come together at the right shoulder
Fists drop to the waist, elbows bent, bouncing in place
Both hands to the left shoulder, then both hands to the right shoulder, finishing with the right arm folded across the chest to the left shoulder

notes: Waist-up framing: reference ankles are NaN in 100% and knees in ~70% of ok frames, so the 'legs' fault never fires on this dance.
'ready' is the count-in: the judge's reference clock starts count_in_s after the first ok learner frame unless set_ref_clock is used. The dancer is already walking backwards during it.
Content ends at 13.7 s (last ok frame 411); frames 412-531 are the TikTok end card with no dancer.

Left/right in move names are screen sides, which the learner mirrors; because the clip is mirrored these are also the dancer's real sides, but the npz COCO labels are swapped (npz left_wrist = screen right = blue skeleton).

The whole group walks backwards away from the camera during 0-4 s, so the reference skeleton shrinks by about 40% over the intro; torso-normalised features handle this but absolute pixel distances do not.
Four dancers in frame; tracker ids 1, 2 and 4 perform the same choreography and the track-2/track-4 npz files exist as alternates.
